title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. In the 'Teichmülleries' notes (1981–83), Grothendieck studies automorphisms of the profinite Teichmüller tower, the kind induced by Gal(Q̄/Q). This page treats the genus-1 one-pointed level, π1(M_{1,1}) = SL(2,Z), and its central extension SL(2,Z)^~. The heading reads roughly 'Ext[ension] des gr. de M_{0,3}[0] dans Sl(2,Z)^ : Sl(2,Z)^{~^}'.

The group. SL(2,Z)^~ is the braid group B_3 = <ρ̃, σ̃ | ρ̃^{-3} = σ̃^2>. The image shows the relation as ρ̃^{-3} = σ̃^2 = ω̃_0, consistent with the later underbrace ρ̃^3 = ω̃_0^{-1}. Here ω̃_0 generates the centre, and ε̃_0 = σ̃ρ̃ is the parabolic ('Dehn twist') generator. He also sets l'_0 = ω̃_0^2. Notation: σ(x) = σ̃xσ̃^{-1} and ρ(x) = ρ̃xρ̃^{-1}.

The automorphism. ũ is a continuous automorphism of the profinite completion of the following type:
- On elliptic generators it acts as conjugation twisted by central scalars: ũ(ρ̃) = λ'·int(α̃)(ρ̃) = λ'ξ̃ρ̃ with ξ̃ = α̃ρ(α̃^{-1}); ũ(σ̃) = λ''·int(β̃)(σ̃) = λ''η̃σ̃ with η̃ = β̃σ(β̃^{-1}). The scalars λ', λ'' are central.
- On the centre it acts cyclotomically: ũ(ω̃_0) = ω̃_0^μ.
- The question is whether the parabolic generator also goes to its μ-th power, ũ(ε̃_0) = ε̃_0^μ (the inertia / 'tangential base point' condition). The top box asserts this is equivalent to a congruence ν' − ν'' = 2ν on auxiliary exponents.

Step 1: the scalars are forced. The struck-out first attempt (λ''^2·η̃σ(η̃) = l_0ω̃_0^{2ν}, etc.) is replaced by the following.
- Cubing: ũ(ρ̃^3) = λ'^3·int(α̃)(ω̃_0^{-1}) = λ'^3ω̃_0^{-ε_3}. Setting this equal to ũ(ω̃_0^{-1}) = ω̃_0^{-μ} gives λ' = ω̃_0^{-(μ−ε_3)/3}.
- Squaring: similarly λ'' = ω̃_0^{(μ−ε_2)/2}.
- Hence λ'λ'' = ω̃_0^{(μ−3ε_2+2ε_3)/6}.
- The ε_i are signs describing how the conjugating elements act on the centre. Divisibility in Ẑ needs μ ≡ ε_3 mod 3 and μ ≡ ε_2 mod 2.

Step 2: the parabolic condition.
- ũ(ε̃_0) = ũ(σ̃)ũ(ρ̃) = λ''η̃σ(λ'ξ̃)ε̃_0. So the condition is λ''η̃σ(λ'ξ̃) = ε̃_0^{μ−1}, written l̃_0^ν with μ−1 = 2ν.
- Since σ̃^2 is central, σ is an involution and σ(η̃) = σ(β̃)β̃^{-1} = η̃^{-1}.
- Transporting by σ gives (λ'λ'')η̃^{-1}ξ̃ = l̃_1^ν.
- Boxed result: (λ'λ'')ξ̃ =? η̃·l̃_1^ν.

What this is. It is the genus-1 analogue of the Drinfeld/GT relations, with exponents (μ−1)/2-type. It converts 'ũ preserves the inertia class of the cusp' into a single cocycle-type equation linking the two conjugating elements at the orbifold points of orders 2 and 3.
errors: The relation is ρ̃^{-3} = σ̃^2 = ω̃_0, not ρ̃^3 = σ̃^2. This matters for the sign of the exponent of λ'.

The side expressions λ' = ω̃_0^{1−2ν''} = l'_0^{1−ν''} and λ'' = ω̃_0^{2ν'} = l'_0^{ν'} are tentative. They are only consistent if (μ−ε_3)/3 and (μ−ε_2)/2 are rewritten with the parameters ν', ν''. The marginal notation is ambiguous and not fully checkable.
In the line for λ'λ'' Grothendieck drops the tilde (ω_0); this is a harmless slip.
The equivalence 'ν'−ν'' = 2ν' in the top box is stated without derivation on this page. Its link to the boxed final equation is left open (marked '?').

ideas.what: Presenting π1 of the orbifold M_{1,1} (and its central extension B_3 = SL(2,Z)^~) by elliptic generators of orders 4 and 6 (lifted) plus a central element, with the cusp generator ε̃_0 = σ̃ρ̃
ideas.modern_name: B_3 as universal central extension of SL(2,Z) / PSL(2,Z) = Z/2*Z/3
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the role of M_{1,1} and SL(2,Z)^ in the Teichmüller tower, but not this computation

ideas.what: Automorphisms of the profinite tower acting on each elliptic generator as a conjugate times a central scalar, with cyclotomic action on the centre; scalars forced to be ω̃_0^{(μ−ε)/n} for n = 2, 3
ideas.modern_name: Galois/GT action on π1(M_{1,1}) in 'special' form; elliptic-point relations of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990) for GT; Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps, Hain–Matsumoto (1990s–2000s) for the genus-1 / SL(2,Z) version

ideas.what: Reducing the condition 'ũ maps the cusp generator to its μ-th power' to the single equation (λ'λ'')ξ̃ = η̃·l̃_1^ν, using that σ is an involution on the group (σ(η̃) = η̃^{-1})
ideas.modern_name: inertia-preservation (tangential base point) condition; analogue of Drinfeld's hexagon/2-cycle relations at level M_{1,1}

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly derives, around 1981–82, the constraints that a 'Galois-type' automorphism of the profinite completion of SL(2,Z)^~ = B_3 must satisfy. The central twists at the elliptic points of orders 3 and 2 are forced to be ω̃_0^{-(μ−ε_3)/3} and ω̃_0^{(μ−ε_2)/2}. The cusp condition reduces to a single equation in the conjugators. This anticipates the genus-1 GT-type relations later written by Nakamura and Lochak–Schneps, which are usually attributed to the 1990s literature.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents Grothendieck's priority in setting up the M_{1,1}-level equations of the Teichmüller tower before Drinfeld's GT. The sign characters ε_2, ε_3 (exponent congruences mod 2 and mod 3) are a detail worth comparing with the published genus-1 GT relations.

missed.claim: Whether the inertia condition at the cusp follows automatically from the elliptic-point data is left open: the final boxed equation carries a '?', as does its claimed equivalence with ν'−ν'' = 2ν.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is the 'special automorphism' issue (inertia preservation) that remains subtle in anabelian / GT theory.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a competent, essentially correct computation of genus-1 GT-type relations by Grothendieck circa 1981–82, predating Drinfeld. Such relations are now standard (Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps), and the page is fragmentary with its key equivalence unproved, so it adds a priority detail rather than new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: Relations: the image reads ρ̃^{-3} = σ̃^2 = ω̃_0, not ρ̃^3 = σ̃^2.
'Edt' at the top is probably 'Ext' (extension) or an abbreviation; the reading is uncertain.
The ũ(ω̃_0) line has a struck initial character; it reads ũ(ω̃_0) = ω̃_0^μ.
The bracketed side equalities next to λ' and λ'' are partially struck/overwritten; λ' = ω̃_0^{-(μ-ε_3)/3} and λ'' = ω̃_0^{(μ-ε_2)/2} are the firm parts.
In the final box, the struck material between (λ'λ'') and '=' is heavily scribbled out; the intended reading is (λ'λ'')ξ̃ ≟ η̃ l̃_1^ν.
The page number written in the corner is 177.
